label: copy-phase input w (fed-back w), from the 3rd original position on
explanation: Fires when the token w is fed back as input during the copy phase (99.9% of mass is copy phase, 100% of mass is in_tok == w). It depends on where w sat in the original sequence (orig position = recall_idx - 1): w from original position >= 3 (recall_idx >= 4) always fires (precision 1.0 on dev); w from position 2 fires about half the time and weakly (~0.3-0.6 of max); w from position 1 fires rarely and weakly; w from position 0 does not fire at all. Activation grows with the w being later in the sequence, and is highest on the 2nd/3rd of consecutive w runs and on w near the end (top examples ~1.0 at the final copy steps). Does not fire on w during the original phase (except a tiny residue) or at the delimiter, and does not fire on any other token, nor on what is being output.

issues: The main claims hold. 99.9% of activation mass is in the copy phase and 100% is on in_tok == w. The original-phase residue is small (dev precision 0.0045 for w in phase 0). The feature never fires at the delimiter, and w at recall_idx 1 never fires (precision 0.0). w at recall_idx >= 4 always fires (precision 1.0, even when to_go >= 4). out_tok has no effect (flat profile).

Systematic gap: whether w fires at recall_idx 2-3 depends on to_go (how many copy steps are left), not on position alone. Dev precision for w at recall_idx 2: to_go 0 -> 1.00, to_go 1 -> 0.95, to_go 2 -> 0.01, to_go 3-5 -> 0.00. For w at recall_idx 3: to_go 0 -> 1.00, to_go 1 -> 1.00, to_go 2 -> 0.875, to_go 3 -> 0.40, to_go 4 -> 0.20, to_go 5 -> 0.28.

So 'position 1 fires rarely and weakly' and 'position 2 fires about half the time' are averages that hide a near-deterministic rule. A w from position 1 (recall_idx 2) fires reliably when it is in the last two copy steps (L <= 4) and never otherwise. A w from position 2 (recall_idx 3) fires reliably when to_go <= 2.

The predicate's false positives are not scattered noise. Most come from w at recall_idx 3 with to_go >= 3, which fires only 20-40% of the time. The predicate also misses all w at recall_idx 2 with to_go <= 1 (about 2.8k dev steps that fire at ~95-100%).

With recall_idx >= 4, or recall_idx 2-3 near the end of the copy, added to the predicate: test precision rises from 0.894 to 0.991, F1 from 0.915 to 0.967, and mass recall from 0.978 to 0.995. The misses that remain are very weak activations (0.00-0.14 of max, 0.5% of mass), mainly early-copy w at recall_idx 3, plus the tiny original-phase residue.
